svg.title: TYPE_REPARK_TRAY / TYPE_MOVE_TRAY -> PlanReparkTrayJob()
svg.desc: Move one tray to a parking node. Two jobs move the same tray, so rule A chains them. Six other job methods create their tray moves through this method.
svg.metadata: ["Start: the request arrives. The map is working_state as the method first sees it; no events yet. Step through the method one table row at a time.", "Row 1. A repark needs at least a tray or a destination; with neither there is nothing to plan. In this example: Both are given. (passes)", "Row 2. Make a scratch copy of the request's garage and apply every event already in the DAG, so the method sees the garage as earlier jobs will leave it. In this example: Job 1 replays event 1, so working_state has T19 at P24. (replay)", "Row 3. Create the TrayMove object now (tagged with job_index) and fill it in step by step; it joins the DAG later. In this example: Created now, added to the DAG at step 10. (not in DAG yet)", "Row 4. Look the tray up and reject unknown or disabled trays. Note: this reads the request snapshot, not the scratch garage. In this example: Both jobs read T19 at P19, the request position, even though job 1's working_state has it at P24. (passes)", "Row 5. A tray on a VECS that is charging must stop charging first; any other non-ready VECS state blocks the job. In this example: P19 has no VECS. (skipped)", "Row 6. Choose the parking heading: an empty tray keeps its heading if that fits; a loaded tray faces the node's retrieval heading so a later retrieve is fast. In this example: Job 0: P24 is parking and T19 carries a car, so the heading becomes P24's retrieval heading. Job 1 has allow_reciprocal = false. (heading set)", "Row 7. If the tray is already at the destination pose, succeed without a move. In this example: Compares with the request position (step 4). Neither job is a no-op. (no early exit)", "Row 8. Reject destinations that are a VECS not ready to charge, not in the graph, disabled for this tray, or a disabled bay. In this example: P24 and P23 are plain, enabled parking. (passes)", "Row 9. Apply the heading policy again for every known tray (EV-charge exception, then retrieval heading), then store the destination. In this example: T19 is loaded, so the retrieval heading of P24 (job 0) or P23 (job 1) is used if that node has a feasible one; Pecos is not 576_eccles, so the EV exception does nothing. (dest set)", "Row 10. Add the TrayMove to the DAG and chain it after this tray's previous event (rule A). In this example: Job 0: T19 has no earlier event. Job 1: T19's last event is 1, so edge 1 -> 2. (adds 1, 2 \u00b7 A)", "Row 11. If the destination is a bay or VECS, also wait for that resource's last event (rule C). In this example: Neither destination is a bay or VECS. (rule C skipped)", "Row 12. Make the move wait for earlier events of the same job (rule B). In this example: Each job has one event: no rule B edge. (no edge)", "Playing the plan (one illustrative execution: AGV assignment and motion planning choose the real AGV and route): AGV-1 drives empty W26 -> P23 -> P19 and stops under T19 (the approach for event 1; AGV assignment adds such moves later).", "Playing the plan: event 1. AGV-1 lifts T19, carries it P19 -> P23 -> P24 and lowers it.", "Playing the plan: event 2. AGV-1 lifts T19, carries it P24 -> P23 and lowers it. No approach drive: AGV-1 is still under T19 after event 1. Every tray and AGV is now where the plan leaves it."]
